concept_name: Naming an angle from its degrees

item.question: Name each angle as acute, right, obtuse or straight: 35°, 90°, 120°, 180°.
steps: 35° is less than 90°, so it is acute.
90° is exactly a quarter turn, so it is a right angle.
120° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.
180° is a half turn, so it is a straight angle.
item.answer: 35° is acute, 90° is right, 120° is obtuse and 180° is straight.
item.text:
Worked example: Name each angle as acute, right, obtuse or straight: 35°, 90°, 120°, 180°.
1. 35° is less than 90°, so it is acute.
2. 90° is exactly a quarter turn, so it is a right angle.
3. 120° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.
4. 180° is a half turn, so it is a straight angle.
Answer: 35° is acute, 90° is right, 120° is obtuse and 180° is straight.

steps_tex: Put the centre of the protractor on the vertex $T$ and the $0$ line along the arm $TP$, then read the scale where each arm crosses it.
$TR$ reads $30^\circ$ and $TQ$ reads $60^\circ$, so $\angle PTR = 30^\circ$ and $\angle PTQ = 60^\circ$; both are less than $90^\circ$, so both are acute.
$TW$ reads $102^\circ$, so $\angle PTW = 102^\circ$, which is more than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$, so it is obtuse.
$\angle WTP$ has the same arms but goes the long way round, so $\angle WTP = 360^\circ - 102^\circ = 258^\circ$.
Check: $\angle PTW + \angle WTP = 102^\circ + 258^\circ = 360^\circ$, a full turn, and $258^\circ$ is more than $180^\circ$, so $\angle WTP$ is reflex.

item.question: Puzzle: I am an acute angle. If you double my measure, you get an acute angle. If you triple my measure, you will get an acute angle again. If you quadruple (four times) my measure, you will get an acute angle yet again! But if you multiply my measure by 5, you will get an obtuse angle measure. What are the possibilities for my measure?
steps_tex: $4 \times$ measure $< 90$, so measure $< 22.5$
$5 \times$ measure $> 90$, so measure $> 18$
Whole degrees between $18$ and $22.5$: $19$, $20$, $21$, $22$
item.answer_tex: The acute angle can be $19^\circ$, $20^\circ$, $21^\circ$ and $22^\circ$ (whole-number degrees).
steps: 4 × measure < 90, so measure < 22.5
